newsitem.title: FRANCE: French privatisation stocks lose over Left's win.
newsitem.headline: French privatisation stocks lose over Left's win.

text.p: Shares in French companies slated for privatisation lost heavily on the Paris bourse on Monday as investors, bereft of clear policy signals, fretted over the advent of a new Socialist-led government.

With little to go on before the left-wing government is up and running, stock market investors opted for caution as they waited to see whether the privatisation plans drawn up by the outgoing centre-right coalition would suffer a setback.

The Socialist party started out with a tough stance against privatisations during the election campaign, but gradually toned down its declarations to the point where people are unsure if it wants to hold up, challenge or abandon the sell-offs that are already in the pipeline.
Shares in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF, in which the centre-right has put its 58 percent stake up for sale, closed 6.99 percent lower at 153.0 francs.
Shares in rival bidders for the Thomson-CSF stake, Lagardere and Alcatel Thomson, also lost ground.
Investment certificates in state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais, a medium-term privatisation candidate after several successive government bailouts, closed 4.17 percent lower at 207 francs.
All suffered in a stock market which otherwise managed to shake off an early dive and close a little higher than before the election runoff vote on Sunday.

The greatest suspense concerns France Telecom after the toppling of a centre-right ruling coalition which planned to sell a minority stake by public offer in what could be the country's biggest ever "privatisation."

France Telecom would not comment on Monday beyond saying it too was waiting to see what how things would evolve with a new administration and the Socialist party said the matter was not discussed at a meeting of its national policy-making committee.
Socialists including party spokesman Francois Hollande said early in the campaign that France Telecom would remain entirely in state hands.
But party leader Lionel Jospin has limited himself to saying staff at the state telecoms operator would be "consulted" before any decision was taken.

The centre-right, which planned to sell a stake of 30-35 percent and possibly raise 30-50 billion francs, postponed the launch of the sell-off from early May to early June as a result of the election.

Some analysts believe the Socialists will need money to recapitalise other firms without adding further pressure to state finances and that this means they will in any case have to at least opt for sales of stakes in state firms -- not strictly speaking privatisations.

Another vicitm of the suspense on Monday was Dassault Aviation, which risks being nationalised if the privatisation of its merger partner Aerospatiale is scuppered, was suspended limit-down on Monday.
Other privatisations whose future is in question include Air France, insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) and its banking subsidiary Credit Industriel et Commercial.
